newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Bordeaux wine exports at all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French Bordeaux wine exports at all-time high.

text.p: Exports of Bordeaux wines hit an all-time high last year, rising by 6 percent in volume and 14 percent in value over the previous year, industry officials said on Monday.
The CIVB Bordeaux wine industry body said that 1.96 million hectolitres (43 million gallons) of Bordeaux were exported in 1996, with a total value of 5.17 billion French francs ($890 million).
The United States bought 115,000 hectolitres (2.53 million gallons) in 1996, an increase of 12 percent over the previous year, while exports to Hong Kong soared by 400 percent.
Europe remained France's biggest Bordeaux customer, accounting for 75 percent of exports. Within that market, Germany was the leading importer.

Bordeaux exports to Scandinavia dropped after Paris staged a series of nuclear weapons tests in the South Pacific in 1995-96. Sales to Norway plunged by 55 percent, while those to Denmark and Sweden were down 32 percent.
Exports of red wine, which accounted for three-quarters of all Bordeaux wine sales abroad, fuelled the increase, climbing 10 percent to 1.46 million hectolitres (32.1 million gallons).
